readme.text:
# ⚓ Midway — 4–7 June 1942 · open-ocean map

**Live:** https://midway1942.vercel.app · **Series:** [Narrated History Map](https://github.com/icomppower/Gundambattleseries) · **Engine:** [cinematic-3d-battle-engine](https://github.com/keithligh/cinematic-3d-battle-engine) by Keith Li (MIT), unmodified

A self-playing 3D documentary of the carrier battle, told as **what each side knew, believed, and got wrong, hour by hour**.
Every caption carries a belief-state chip — KNOWN · BELIEVED (IJN) · BELIEVED (USN) · UNKNOWN · DISPUTED — and reported-but-wrong
contacts are drawn as ghost markers beside the actual ones. Bilingual 繁體中文 / English.

This fork breaks four engine assumptions (no terrain, a 1,300 nm box, the antimeridian, fog of war) — the reasoning for each
is in **[DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md)**. Planning, research brief and A/B protocol live in Notion (source of truth).

## Run locally
```
python3 tools/build_tiles.py    # fetches the 180 source bathymetry tiles (cached) and builds lib/tiles/ (already committed)
node tools/serve.js             # http://localhost:5050  (file:// will not work)
node tools/validate.mjs && node tools/check-agnostic.mjs
```
Do **not** run `tools/fetch_tiles.mjs` for this box — the box crosses 180° and this fork's tiles are generated, not fetched (DECISIONS.md §1, §3).

## Deploy
`vercel --prod --force` (Static HTML preset). `--force` is required: incremental deploys drop unchanged tiles.

## Credits
Built by [Johnny Lai](https://www.linkedin.com/in/icomppower/). Engine by Keith Li (MIT). Bathymetry: AWS Terrain Tiles (Mapzen Terrarium; ETOPO1/GEBCO). Sources are listed in the Notes panel and in `data.js`.
